text:
marta: FYI — seeing a sudden spike of 5xx and streaming timeouts hitting /v1/generate in us-west-2 around 11:03 UTC. Error rate ~12% and p90 latency ~2.4s -> 6s. Starting war room. @kevin @sam @ivy
kevin: on it, joining now. any obvious deploys in the last 30m?
sam: I see a canary deploy finished ~10:58 but traffic should be pinned. looking at traces now.
opsbot: Incident created: hosted-inference-timeouts-us-west-2. Priority: P1. Paging: oncall-eng-sre.
ivy: checking batcher metrics — backlog on batcher-queue-3 spiked, queue depth x4. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 74%.
leo: also seeing increased 502s at the edge, NLB connection resets spike correlated to same window.
marta: good catch. sam, can you correlate trace ids to runtime errors?
sam: quick grep of traces: lots of "upstream reset" and "context deadline exceeded" from runtime pods. some 5xx have cause "batcher timeout" in logs.
kevin: rolling back the small change from 10:58 (canary autoscaler tweak) to be safe. deploying rollback now — ETA ~6m.
ivy: prefiring mitigation: turning on circuit-breaker to route heavy traffic to eu-fallback for non-enterprise customers. pushing policy patch.
leo: support-bot posting to customers: delayed responses, working on it.
support-bot: Public message queued for affected customers, minimal template.
kevin: rollback started. health checks failing on a couple pods, restarting them one-by-one.
sam: pulling logs from a repro pod: 
```
ERROR runtime: batcher timeout after 15000ms; kv cache miss for prefix id=abc123; upstream conn reset
```
marta: sounds like combination: cache warmup regression + canary autoscaler change made batch sizes/liveness misaligned -> queue backlog -> timeouts.
ivy: increasing batcher workers temporarily (+30%) and disabling the new autoscaler heuristic. applied now.
kevin: rollback finished. new deploy healthy after restarts. error rate dropping: from 12% -> 1.8% over last 5m.
leo: NLB resets subsided after pod restarts. p95 latency back to ~800ms.
marta: excellent. next: collect repro, root-cause notes, and action items.
sam: repro steps (short): send 40k small requests at 50rps with prefix-skew to /v1/generate -> observe kv miss amplification -> batcher queue grows -> backend timeouts. attaching sample script to thread.
kevin: immediate actions we did: rollback autoscaler tweak, restart unhealthy runtime pods, increase batcher workers, route non-critical traffic to EU fallback for 20m.
ivy: monitoring: added alert rule for KV cache hit-rate drop >10% sustained and batcher queue depth >200 for 3m.
leo: support follow-up: notified impacted customers with incident id, offered SLA credit assessment if needed.
marta: postmortem owners: sam (RCA writeup), kevin (deploy gating + rollout process), ivy (batcher autoscaling and cache warmup), leo (customer comms + SLA assessment). Due EOD tomorrow.
sam: probable root cause: the autoscaler heuristic change reduced prewarmed batcher capacity during a short traffic pattern, exposing a cache warmup regression in the new runtime image. Both changes coincided -> amplification.
kevin: action items (short):
- revert heuristic (done)
- add canary traffic pinning for batcher/autoscaler (owner: kevin)
- add synthetic cache-warmup step in deploy pipeline (owner: ivy)
- tighten rollout window and increase monitoring pre/post (owner: kevin)
- create runbook for rapid fallback to eu region (owner: leo)
ivy: I'll also add a regression test that simulates prefix-skew and measures KV hit-rate under ramp.
marta: timeline summary: 11:03 detect -> 11:06 war room -> 11:09 rollback start -> 11:16 rollback complete -> 11:23 steady recovery. impact: elevated 5xx and timeouts for ~20m, affecting ~3% of hosts and a subset of customers on us-west-2.
support-bot: Incident status: mitigated. postmortem required.
kevin: will open a follow-up ticket with deploy gating checklist and link to logs/traces. ticket: INF-4528.
sam: attaching sample traces and the small repro script to the ticket.
marta: thanks all — we can close this war room thread. please update ticket with action item progress. :white_check_mark:
